title: Distinguish invocation names from application file locations
goal: Choose invocation identity for command aliases and physical-location APIs for executable or managed-file diagnostics, including unavailable bundled locations.

selectionNotes: Choose invocation identity for command aliases and physical-location APIs for executable or managed-file diagnostics, including unavailable bundled locations.
Older examples are comparisons, not additional catalogue targets.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: The primary route uses the net11.0 framework/package asset and .NET 11 behavior.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Build the declared net11.0 consumer with a matching SDK.

language.name: C#
language.reason: The canonical .NET 11 project selects C# 15; the comparison project selects C# 14.

packageAssets: Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref ref/net11.0 and Microsoft.NETCore.App runtime; framework-supplied APIs, no added NuGet package
platforms: Desktop/server .NET. Proof: Windows 11 x64/NTFS with real symlink permission; cmd.exe relative launch and framework-dependent single-file publication. No Unix/browser/WASI proof.
prerequisites: Console project with implicit usings and System.Reflection; apphost invocation identity requires launching the apphost. Alias reproduction requires real symbolic-link capability.
constraints: Launcher spelling can be normalized; do not promise identical relative names for every launcher. Never execute a reconstructed argv[0] path.
ProcessPath can be null; entry Location can be null/empty and is empty for bundled assemblies. None defines an application data directory.
stabilityLimitations: Exact RC2 artifacts executed; no GA verification. No experimental annotation or opt-in on the used APIs.

evidence.scope: Canonical invocation/location report and bounded help aliases; actual selected runtime and compiler/ref artifacts.
